why: After sorting, every optimal order builds its prefix as a contiguous window of the sorted values that grows by one element on the left or the right. So it is interval DP: dp[l][r] = (a[r]-a[l]) + min(dp[l+1][r], dp[l][r-1]). The week's greedy + sorting gives the sorted view, but plain greedy (sorted order) is not always optimal.
hints: Sort first. If the first i products chosen are not a contiguous block of the sorted array, can you swap something to lower the sum?
Every prefix of an optimal arrangement is a contiguous window a[l..r] of the sorted array, and the next product extends that window by one on the left or on the right.
dp over windows: dp[l][r] = a[r] - a[l] + min(dp[l+1][r], dp[l][r-1]), with dp[i][i] = 0. Iterate by window length with a rolling 1-D array. O(n^2) time, O(n) memory, fine for n = 2000.
pitfalls: Just sorting ascending or descending is not optimal; you must be able to extend on either side.
Equal values cost nothing, so duplicates naturally group; no special handling is needed after sorting.
